title: China Issues Draft Regulations on AI Copyright Infringement
key_facts: The Cyberspace Administration of China released the draft 'Administrative Measures for Digital Virtual Human Information Services' on April 3; public comment was open until May 6.
It follows complaints from actors, influencers and ordinary people that their likenesses were stolen for AI short dramas.

Companies would need consent from the people whose images they use (from parents or guardians for minors) and must delete related personal information if consent is withdrawn; the draft also requires respect for portrait and reputation rights and forbids caricatures and disparagement.

A day earlier the Actors Committee of the China Federation of Radio and Television Associations condemned unauthorised AI voice cloning and face swapping, and said labelling content 'non-commercial' gives no exemption.

Hongguo, a short-drama app owned by ByteDance, removed hundreds of videos in the first quarter of 2026 over stolen AI likenesses; the 72-episode drama 'Peach Blossom Hairpin' had over 41 million views before being taken down on March 31.
On April 6 the studios of actors Zhang Jingyi and Deng Wei said their images were used without authorisation and that lawyers are collecting evidence.
Tech insiders say it is hard to decide what counts as AI infringement; proving a voice was stolen is often a 'percentage question'.
quote_evidence: Released April 3 by the Cyberspace Administration of China, the draft “Administrative Measures for Digital Virtual Human Information Services” is open for public commentary until May 6.
The draft states that companies would first need to obtain consent from the individuals whose images they seek to use and, in cases involving minors, from their parents or guardians.
determining whether a voice has been stolen by AI is often a “percentage question” rather than a clear-cut “yes or no.”
why_it_matters_hint: China is moving to give people a legal say over AI copies of their faces and voices, but this is a draft.
event_date: Draft released 3 Apr 2026; comments until 6 May 2026.
